entry.title: The NPCs in this Village Sim Game Must Be Real!
entry.content:
This is my fourth light novel that I'm reading in a good flow, my first has been Three days of happiness and then If cats disappeared from world and third is Apothecary Diaries (ongoing) and now I've liked on NPC Town-building Game novel.

I stumbled on this one in r/LightNovels post (don't ask me why), since it was a small series I definitely took a favor to read it next. After writing down I've Consumed Enough I'm leaning more towards reading book or textual content more (hopefully no slop, everything predating 2023-era). Because the greatest minds have always transcribed knowledge in that way, and the only source of truth are by books.

As Divjot (DJ) said in one of Indie Club meeting, we humans are all about moving stone/rocks from one place to another. I'd also like to add, changing one form to another as well (obviously cannot forget the classic law).

I was not looking for self-improvement per-say here, but was more wanting for a Mindful reading than a mindless rot. This novel is only of three volumes, and I completed the first volume within a day and second volume half completed, the writing (translation) was very apt and easy to grasp. This is not an Isekai story or OP stuffs thrown everywhere. The story is about a NEET person who got a game to play and that game is very realistic that every moment feels alive and lively to his own life (uhh, thats one way to interpret), go check info page that gives synopsis and reviews for more clarity, I'm here to only interpret and make notes.

IDK how to even write this post, but I'll just make a list of good things that was nice to read:

  • I like how Inspecting/Simulation of others lives helps Yoshio to realize his own life and get inspired and get directed ahead.
  • Its a slow, steady and heart warming story, unlike any other novel, this goes in two place; one is virtual sim village game which is middle age scenario and second is Yoshio's IRL japan village with his family.
  • I really like how novel showed that things can be fixed easily even after long time, how yoshio life was getting fixed with his family and himself.
  • Novel author - Hirukuma, portrayed more real life struggles and bad habits in digital world clearly showcasing how gacha games and its world run micro-transactions and trap humans.
  • TBH even I felt that if NPCs can be simulated that way realistically, why can't we humans also do it. We got so habituated with automation now that we are watching Sim games to have fun? The real fun is in doing stuff and not watching (same goes for GTA VI, but dont blame me for theft)
  • I also like how contrasting a simulated (imaginary) world in middle age can be and how modern today's life is in this novel. Yoshio always relates and learn through them all along.
  • Portrayal of God was phenomenal in some ways, I like how NPCs also dont depend on God alot and are just grateful for being watched, but still they put in their 100% efforts and take care of themselves.
  • This is how a novel must be written and finished. I really like when authors decide how and when it ends, without playing fan service to the end and fillers. Every character had their role as NPCs and even IRL humans shown.
  • I'm really happy that I'd imagine some scenario by reading this and not crave for illustration, thinking is really amazing.

Also apart from reading joy, I felt very much interested to write a light-novel myself, I just felt like even I can create a world with my own stories of adventure, as I said in my prev post that I've already consumed enough, so I should start creating stuff on top of it. I know this will be a long process, but thanks to this mindful reading session I'll start to write some form of small stories and publish it on my site as same blog posts itself, typically tag as #webnovel or #story. I know nobody cares nor reads, but I may so write to let my mind and imagination be at peace. I'm a big fan of One Piece (yk it already), and I want to read LOTM soon as well, so you'd imagine what kinda big novel world even I want to build. But although I get peak motivated, I just get cooled off thinking that I need to learn more and read more from greatest work to produce worthy content, but who knows, once i start things can escalate to new level (lets hope).

For more context or review, you may check Sean Gaffney's blog post

Note: I've written this after reading volume 1 completely and half on volume 2, so soon will finish second and third volume and write a followup below.

entry.title: If cats disappeared from world
entry.content:
If Cats Disappeared from the World is an light novel by Genki Kawamura.

It depicts the life-death situation of a person, who in-return to live a day makes something disappear from the world. The novel shows a thought-provoking idea of, "what's life worth it" or how much meaning it carries.

The reviews spoke as sober one, but I did not feel any depressing moment about story. But the lesson and points definitely are reflective on life. The major good thing about the book is, English translation and writing style is easy and friendly. I would not recommend movie as such, but the gist is shown very well there

The ending was kinda cliffhanger, but did not end as in climax. It suddenly closed off. Again I think back, it seemed that the book itself might be the letter he was writing for his father or in some way. But sure ending is confusing.

Three days of happiness and this one is kinda one of my best reads.

entry.title: Three days of happiness
entry.content:
A light novel by the name, and manga goes by name Jumyou wo Kaitotte Moratta. Ichinen ni Tsuki, Ichimanen de by Sugaru Miaki. His all novels follow similar theme.

If you wonder why japanese manga names are reallyyy long, they say that, its useful for buyers to know the gist of what it is about. So basically the names would indicate most of the main theme or gist. It makes sense as it can gives mini-overview on itself.

The story is kinda depressing, or lets say it makes you sober. More of its an thought provoking story and makes you wonder the importance in life. Although everyone cannot relate based on NEET character, since IRL we are busy with connections and responsibilities and some flow is going on with out life.

This manga/LN left me with lots of questions and lots of thoughts. Wonderful depiction of love, life and the worthwhile of doing things. In fact, last (extra) chapter was so valuable that gave another perspective of living.

Lot of take in, but many were indirectly spoken. The focus might seem on lifespan, love and death. But the key takeaway would be on passion, interests and career.

Socializing came a bit and flew away, but still seemed positive.

This might be my beginning for loving these kinda manga, of understanding life and maybe kick start reading light novels.

Good for nothing was the main theme, but it depicts that it vanishes when loved ones are together.

First time I did not feel much, but reading some pages again felt more pain. After reading this one, I went on searching similar one just like this, but unfortunately nothing like this. This feels different unlike any for me. I wish I could have started off with light novel, but maybe pictures only gave me more value and more comprehension.
